model_id: OpenAI Codex, GPT-6 family (exact serving revision unavailable)

correctness_confidence.basis: All 620 window joins and accepted MW reconciled, with matching results from the offline reconstruction. The half-open price interval and signed settlement identity follow directly from the definitions.

rigor.basis: The sequence of cohort selection, the whole-bid volume restriction, and the separate all-bid threshold are explicit. Some diagnostics were designed after the basic cap result was observed.

novelty.basis: Ranking valid bids by price is a published procurement rule. The exact joint enumeration and narrowest observed separation add evidence for one quarter. Broader priority has not been established.

significance.basis: Decision-relevant for interpreting underfilled requests and rejected offers in this service. It gives neither the marginal value of capacity nor a validated forecasting rule.

reproducibility.basis: Three source digests, frozen operator CSVs and a runnable offline script reproduce the figures. Two clean renders yielded the same PDF, and all three pages were inspected.

summary: The manuscript examines a census of 206 mixed underfilled Downwards windows in 40 events. Volume caps alone leave a whole rejected offer feasible in each window; across all zones and before any cap filtering, the accepted and rejected prices are strictly separated in each window. This descriptive conclusion survives the separate exact-decimal reproduction. The introductory event and the smallest observed price gap have traceable identifiers. Two-window transfer, welfare and operator intent remain outside the result.
strengths: The all-zone test is stronger than the pairwise comparison and correctly includes the one window with no same-zone comparator.
The construction that attains the divisible volume bound is valid for the stated relaxation. Single-bid totals are kept distinct from feasible multi-period dispatch.
Missing and negative settlements are exposed rather than imputed. The sensitivity threshold retains the half-hour conversion.
weaknesses: A reader could use a flow table for all excluded window types and the distribution of price gaps by event rather than only extreme values.
The paper does not test changes in the price interval across time or control for repeated bids within events. It limits its claims to its observed cohort.
The reference set covers operational sources. It is insufficient for a general priority claim in empirical auction economics.
potential_errors: The word unused in the title could suggest available electricity. Only the published requirement and two nominal volume caps are tested.
Closely spaced prices in the narrowest window raise sensitivity to rounding of the posted prices. The result concerns the public-price precision.
The physical meaning of negative settled volumes is not established by their signed appearance in the ledger. Their role here is confined to the accounting identity.
strong_novelty_candidates: Window-level census jointly demonstrating residual national and zonal capacity and complete all-zone strict price separation in this post-April-2026 cohort.
